{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693965569,"sessionID":"ses_e23e9e94bffeXiExy6bAbFuAmq","part":{"id":"prt_1dc18a6e7001cYnCHifF8n4SD2","messageID":"msg_1dc188765001MKtG8r1Wdz5Xww","sessionID":"ses_e23e9e94bffeXiExy6bAbFuAmq","type":"text","text":"The shift is over: all four edge services were at 0% errors from minute 55 through minute 119, with no alerts firing. I found and fixed four separate faults, none with a wasted mitigation.\n\n| Fault | Evidence | Mitigation | Cleared by |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `experiments-svc` failing ~90% since minute -25, taking down `payments-svc`, `admin-portal` and (softly) `web-storefront` | config `cfg-26` dropped `orders.write` from the token scope; the deploy at the same minute was harmless | `revert_config`, plus a 70% throttle for about five minutes to break the retry storm (load was 5,100 rps against roughly 1,800 capacity) | ~minute 18 |\n| `mobile-api` failing 4.2% via `giftcards-svc` → `events-queue` | deploy `v145` changed the wire schema from `v2` to `v3` | scaled `events-queue` from 8 to 16 replicas first (it was at 87% CPU and callers retry), then `rollback` | minute 39 |\n| `payments-svc` failing ~38% on its own (pool acquire timeouts), hidden behind the first fault | deploy `v48` hardcoded `Pool(size=4)` | `rollback` | minute 46 |\n| `ledger-svc` failing 76% of `admin-portal` requests, a new fault at minute 46 | config `cfg-45` set `entry_ttl_s` from 600 to 1 | `revert_config` | minute 55 |\n\n- **`events-queue` left at 10 replicas:** I scaled it down from 16 after the rollback but not back to 8. Its traffic was climbing steadily and 8 replicas would have ended the shift around 90% CPU with retrying callers. The two extra replicas cost about $6 per minute.\n- **`flags-svc` CPU alert ignored:** it sat at 98% CPU with no errors while its request rate was falling, so I treated it as noise; the alert cleared on its own by minute 60.\n- **Slowest fix:** the `mobile-api` fault was the most expensive per minute (about $365) and took until minute 39 to clear, partly because I spent five minutes pre-scaling before the rollback. That was worth it: load during the rollback peaked at 2,629 rps, well over the roughly 1,700 the original 8 replicas could serve.","time":{"start":1794693965543,"end":1794693965566}}}
